links.targetTitle: Spark's collateral is deployed into direct competitors of it

title: Spark pays Aave weekly to hold USDS, choosing distribution through a rival lending market over exclusivity
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1 configures an Integration Boost Primitive Instance whose partner is Aave (A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.1.1), paying rewards to a specified Aave reward address on Ethereum Mainnet (A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.1.2, A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.1.3) on a weekly cadence (A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.1.4).

The strategic content is in who the counterparty is. Aave is the largest competitor to SparkLend, Spark's own lending market. Spark is nonetheless paying it to carry USDS.

That follows from the two-sided mandate: driving USDS adoption is a distribution objective, and the largest pools of DeFi liquidity are not on Spark's own venues. A stablecoin issuer that only incentivizes its own front end caps its adoption at its own market share. Paying rival venues buys reach that the issuer cannot build itself.

The trade-off is honest and visible in the Artifact: the same balance sheet subsidizes both a competitor's deposits and Spark's own lending market, and USDS held in Aave earns Aave fees rather than SparkLend fees. Sky is choosing stablecoin ubiquity over protocol-level capture, which only makes sense because the issuer's return comes from the collateral backing USDS rather than from the venue where USDS sits.
description: The Integration Boost sends rewards to a named Aave address on Ethereum Mainnet on a weekly cadence — Sky subsidizes a direct SparkLend competitor because reach beats containment.
